explanation: Body falls obliquely onto the top corner of a thin vertical wall (wall x 14-14.3, top y=8.3). Steps 22-24 and frames show grazing corner contact: distance goes +0.098 to -0.051 to -0.200 while vx stays constant at -3.24 and vy follows gravity only, i.e. no contact impulse or adequate positional correction is applied at the corner/end-cap. Penetration therefore grows monotonically past the 0.15 limit. Likely cause is corner/edge normal handling for thin boxes: side-vs-top disambiguation misses or under-corrects, letting the circle sink into the corner.
vision_note: The red ball falls straight down onto the top end of the thin vertical wall. It makes contact and then visibly sinks into the tip by step 24 without bouncing or deflecting.
